text:
Ford Motor Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
Key Takeaways
- Positive Sentiment: Q3 adjusted EBIT rose 3% to $2.7 billion, supported by strong truck and SUV mix, cost reductions, and record auto-adjacent revenue. Ford raised the low end of its 2026 adjusted EBIT guidance, now expecting $10.5 billion to $11 billion.
- Positive Sentiment: Ford Pro and Ford Credit remained important earnings contributors, with Ford Pro generating $1.7 billion of EBIT and Ford Credit posting $803 million of EBT. Software services and parts contributed about 10% of quarterly revenue at accretive margins, while Ford Pro expects growth from Oakville capacity and commercial leasing.
- Positive Sentiment: Ford Energy reported strong early demand for grid-scale battery storage, with executed contracts and late-stage negotiations covering more than 80% of expected 2028 capacity. The company remains on track to bring 20 gigawatt-hours of annual capacity online by the end of 2027, with roughly two-thirds of its planned $2 billion investment expected next year.
- Neutral Sentiment: Ford’s affordable Fathom EV remains on track for a late-2027 launch with a starting price of $28,350, and 90% of validation testing is complete. However, supply-base readiness remains a key remaining risk, and Model e is expected to incur higher expenses in 2027 before profitability improves more substantially in 2028-2029.
- Negative Sentiment: Ford expects 2027 profitability to be roughly in line with 2026 despite investments in new vehicles, the Universal EV platform, and Ford Energy. Management anticipates approximately $2 billion of headwinds from commodities, memory, and logistics, while European operations continue to face pressure from Chinese competition, EV mandates, and industry overcapacity.

Good day, everyone. My name is Ronnie and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome you to the Ford Motor Company third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speaker's remarks, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question during this time, please use the raise hand function, which can be found on the black bar at the bottom of your screen. At this time, I would like to turn the call over to Maria Ricciardone, Chief Investor Relations Officer.
Thank you, Ronnie, and welcome to Ford Motor Company's third quarter 2026 earnings call. I'm Maria Ricciardone, Ford Chief Investor Relations Officer. With me today are Jim Farley, President and CEO, and Sherry House, CFO. Joining us for Q&A are Andrew Frick, President of Ford Blue and Model e, Alicia Boler Davis, President of Ford Pro, Kumar Galhotra, Chief Operating Officer, Cathy O'Callaghan, CEO of Ford Credit, and Dave Carroll, President of Ford Energy. Jim will give a high-level overview of the business, and Sherry will provide added texture on the financials and guidance. We will be referencing non-GAAP measures today. These are reconciled to the most comparable U.S. GAAP measures in the appendix of our earnings deck. You can find the deck at shareholder.ford.com. Our discussion also includes forward-looking statements. Our actual results may differ. The most significant risk factors are included on page 20 of our deck.
Unless otherwise noted, all comparisons are year-over-year. Company EBIT, EPS, and free cash flow are on an adjusted basis. Upcoming IR engagements include Sherry House at the Barclays Global Auto and Mobility Tech Conference in New York on November 18th. Now I'll turn the call over to Jim.
Thanks, Maria. Ford delivered another strong quarter, thanks to our great products, our services, and execution. I want to thank our employees and our dealers, all of our suppliers, for this progress and for their commitment to Ford+. In the third quarter, as you know, we generated $2.7 billion in adjusted EBIT. We're raising our low end of our previous full-year adjusted EBIT guidance and now expect to earn between $10.5 billion and $11 billion. Our strategy is clear. Number one, grow our auto business with a whole new generation of vehicles focused on North America, focused on transforming our EV business, and global products with much less capital. Number two, aggressively expand our auto adjacencies, software, services, and parts while strengthening our financing capability. And third, diversifying with Ford Energy.
The objective is a more profitable, capital-efficient, and resilient Ford, one that achieves 8% adjusted EBIT margins by 2029 and delivers sustained earnings, cash flow, and returns to our shareholders over time. Let's start with our vehicles. In the third quarter, we continue to focus on a portfolio that leans into our strengths, trucks, vans, and utilities. Our pickup lineup gives customers an unmatched breadth of choice between vehicles, prices, trims, and powertrains. In Q3, F-Series captured the highest retail share among all full-size truck brands and is on pace for the 50th straight year as America's best-selling truck. Maverick is America's best-selling hybrid pickup. Internationally, Ranger leads in many markets, including Australia and Europe. Early demand for the Ranger Super Duty is very strong. Already number one in heavy-duty medium-sized truck market in Australia in its first year, opening a very profitable opportunity for us.
Transit continues to be the best-selling van in the U.S. Ford also leads in three-row SUVs in the U.S. with the Expedition and Explorer. We're also expanding access to customers through [Ford Blue Advantage], our certified pre-owned program, making Ford now the number one certified pre-owned brand in the U.S. This program builds customer loyalty and positions Ford for our affordable new vehicles that will be coming in the next couple of years to our showrooms, and it really helps our resale values. In fact, we found that these used customers are 50% more likely than typical used car buyers to purchase a new Ford. The foundation of our sustained growth is world-class quality. Of course, topping the JD Power 2026 IQS study and reduction we've seen in warranty coverages is encouraging to all of us.
Excluding Novelis and tariffs, we reduced warranty and material costs by $1.5 billion in 2025 and are on track to reduce another $1 billion this year. But we have much more to do, especially on long-term durability and the ownership experience. We are accelerating our industrial system, including very aggressive next-generation vehicle cost reduction targets. The goal is a world-class industrial system, one that makes cost competitiveness and quality repeatable. Our Super Duty launch in Oakville, Ontario, is an important example of this discipline. The production ramp is already exceeding planned daily volume and jobs per hour rates. We reached okay to buy last week and began shipping trucks to dealerships. The quality we're seeing is fully competitive with our existing Super Duty plant, which is number one in JD Power.
The added capacity will give us flexibility for future plant changeovers and support profitable growth in retail, rental, and outfitter channels. We're bringing the same discipline to the next-generation F-150. Prototypes builds are beginning in the first quarter of 2027, just a couple of months away. We have an incredible powertrain durability testing, which is now a fivefold increase to meet our bulletproof powertrain target at Ford. We're doubling endurance and strength testing and increasing full-vehicle test mileage by nearly 60% to almost 4 million miles. The F-150 will be the most extensively tested truck ever at Ford, and we will apply this exact same approach across our company. Alongside strengthening our best franchises, we're opening new paths to grow at more affordable price points. Next year, we will be launching our affordable midsize pickup for international markets.
We expect the base material cost for this truck to be 20% lower than today's Ranger. Just as Maverick has done in the U.S., this truck is designed to bring new customers into the Ford truck lineup internationally at a cost structure that allows us to compete, in this case, with the Chinese. In Louisville, we are preparing the launch of the Fathom, our first vehicle off the UEV platform. Rigorous testing and early supplier preparation are central to that effort. The launch remains on track for the fourth quarter of next year. Yet yesterday, I had the opportunity to drive our prototype. Wow! It completely blew me away. The 0-60, huge room inside, and the hands-free ADAS experience was like something I've never experienced. Fathom is really a breakthrough product.
It's highly capable, innovative, affordable, and that EV product will be available to more Americans way ahead of our competition. This will require high-level execution by our team to deliver on time and at cost. The MSRP under $30,000 and the low cost of ownership is perfect for today's market. Fathom will offer something brand new for U.S. EV customers, an advanced zonal electrical architecture for its first 48 V low-voltage system, along with a sophisticated advanced driver-assist capability, such as hands-free driving, an incredible rear-wheel drive performance feel, and a lot of fun to drive, and bi-directional charging, so you can power your home with the Fathom when rates are high or during an outage. There's so much more to this product that we're exciting to share with you. Switching gears to our growing auto services business, software services, parts, and financing.
These auto adjacencies deepen our customers' relationship with us and create downstream value by enabling us to earn more over the life of each vehicle. Both software services and parts businesses achieved record revenue in the third quarter at highly accretive margins. An important linkage exists here between software and parts. Connected services help us anticipate maintenance over time, including a whole new software product called Prognostics at Ford, bringing customers to our remote service vans, almost 5,000 of them now, and our dealer network to keep their vehicles running 24/7. We found that when a retail customer combines a software subscription with regular service, the retention of the customer, especially for parts, is about nine points higher. In parts specifically, we grew our U.S. wholesale business to third-party independent repair shops, and we've expanded a lot in Europe.
A broader Motorcraft catalog also allows us to serve fleet customers of competitive brands and owners of much older Ford vehicles. Ford Credit has had a great third quarter. Notably, together with Ford Pro, Credit launched Ford Pro Leasing in the third quarter. It's a big deal for Pro. Adding commercial leasing to our fleet management software and maintenance offerings will help us grow our Pro digital fleet management portfolio, which we will expect to be over 100,000 units by year-end. Many of those are non-Ford vehicles. Turning to Ford Energy, the investment thesis is very clear. Ford is going to solve a meaningful customer problem, build on Ford's advantage, and offer a credible path to material earnings with attractive returns in the short term. Our starting point is U.S.-manufactured grid-scale battery storage for companies building America's new power infrastructure and data centers.
These customers need a domestic partner with the manufacturing know-how and scale and staying power to support them throughout the product's life. We are progressing on two fronts, preparing our manufacturing capacity and securing customers. At our battery plant in Kentucky, we have met every single operating milestone so far. We have completed trial runs of electrode mixing, the first step in producing prismatic LFP battery cells, using the exact same process as our battery plant in Marshall, Michigan. We remain on track to bring 20 GWh of annual capacity online by the end of next year. Commercial progress is encouraging and demand remains very strong. Executed contracts and late-stage negotiations together already currently account for more than 80% of Ford Energy's 2028 capacity.
We are building a diverse customer base across solar, grid support, and data centers, and we expect our 2028 capacity to be fully committed by Q1 of next year. Pricing signals remain consistent with our investment assumptions. Negotiation for 2029 and 2030 capacity are already advancing, with customers engaged way ahead of our initial expectations. The DC Block gives us a practical starting point to build a broader capability. We expect attractive returns with short payback period, as I said. Sherry now is going to take you through our financial performance.
Thank you, Jim, and hello, everyone. Our third quarter results reflect the deliberate actions we're taking to improve profitability and deliver consistent financial returns. Our increasingly fit industrial system, coupled with strong vehicle sales and auto adjacency performance, enable adjusted EBIT growth of 3%, despite 2% lower revenue as we sunset products like Escape and Corsair to transition the Louisville assembly plant for the all-new Fathom. Sequentially, revenue at $49.5 billion in adjusted EBIT at $2.7 billion were both higher, despite being impacted by a short-term supplier disruption late in the quarter. We also generated $4.7 billion in company-adjusted free cash flow in Q3 and ended the quarter with $25.3 billion in cash and $46.4 billion in total liquidity, maintaining our commitment to a strong investment-grade rating into returning capital to shareholders. Today, we announced a fourth-quarter regular dividend of $0.15 per share.
This strong performance reflects the underlying quality of the sales accomplishments Jim mentioned, as well as our progress toward a leaner, more fit industrial system. We continue to see mix strength in trucks and three-row SUVs. Our higher-margin off-road performance products accounted for about a quarter of our U.S. sales in Q3, up almost four points from a year ago, and our customers have been resilient amid higher fuel prices, interest rates, and inflation. We also continue to deliver efficiencies across the business, including the use of AI in our business segments and throughout our operations. These actions, together with our industrial improvements, have helped us absorb the vast majority of headwinds from the Middle East conflict and rising commodity costs. It is this discipline and operational rigor that is taking root across Ford.
In fact, it is directly benefiting our next-generation product pipeline, where we are making real progress in improving the cost base across our products. In addition, the traction in warranty and material cost improvement is strong again this year. Both were lower in the quarter and year-to-date, keeping us firmly on plan towards reducing these costs by $1 billion this year, excluding Novelis and tariffs. We are leveraging these reductions to fund our investments in a Universal Electric Vehicle platform and Ford Energy. At Novelis, operationally, the recovery is largely behind us. Financially, we have incurred about $1 billion in Novelis-related temporary costs year-to-date, with some more to go in Q4, and we are still tracking to a net tailwind of about $1 billion in 2026. Now let's turn to our segment results.
In Ford Blue, we delivered $27.1 billion of revenue and $1.4 billion in EBIT, down 3% and 10% respectively. Our performance primarily reflects lower volume driven by product discontinuations and the impact of the Middle East conflict within the region and higher commodity costs. Our underlying business continues to benefit from favorable mix. We saw significant year-to-date demand in the U.S. for Explorer, with the higher-margin Tremor and Platinum series increasing sales by nearly 60%. F-Series performed well as we executed a disciplined go-to-market approach that yielded the highest share of revenue and lowest incentive spend in the third quarter. Lincoln also had an impressive quarter, with both Nautilus and Aviator experiencing double-digit sales growth in the U.S. Our stock levels are healthy. We ended the quarter slightly below our target range of 55-65 retail days supply, and we increased gross stocks by about 6% versus Q2 2026.
Our F-150 inventory improved quarter-over-quarter to 49 retail days supply, though is still below our ideal range, which provides us with upside as we work to restock to target levels. Overall, we expect stocks to return within our targeted levels by year-end. For Model e, we improved EBIT by 25% year-over-year in the quarter. We reported an EBIT loss of $1.1 billion on revenue of $1.2 billion. These results reflect our focus on capital efficiency and structural cost reductions as we realize the benefits from right-sizing our Gen one volumes while we continue to invest in our UEV platform and Ford Energy. We are on track to improve Gen one EBIT by approximately 40% year-over-year in 2026 as we balance production and pricing with natural demand. In fact, in Q3, Mustang Mach-E had the lowest incentive spend since 2023.
Importantly, we are still targeting breakeven by 2029. Ford Pro delivered another solid quarter with $17.8 billion of revenue, up 2%, despite wholesale volumes being down 4%. Pro EBIT was $1.7 billion, down 16%, primarily due to higher commodities and temporary costs associated with the Oakville launch. Lower tariffs and favorable product mix, driven by higher truck production as we recover from Novelis, partially offset these headwinds. 2027 model year signals are favorable, as most commercial agreements are complete, with both fleet demand and pricing in line with our expectations. Ford Credit delivered a great quarter, with EBT of $803 million, up $172 million. These results reflect favorable performance on our derivatives, healthy financing margins, and a supported used vehicle pricing environment. Our high-quality portfolio of offerings across Ford Credit remains resilient, and we maintain a consistent, disciplined approach to risk management.
Jim talked earlier about the record quarter for software services and parts. I would like to double-click on that. These auto-adjacent businesses were significant drivers of the quarter's strong performance, contributing approximately 10% of the quarter's revenue at strong margins. The largest contributors to software services revenue growth in the quarter and year-to-date were BlueCruise and Connectivity, and we continue to see momentum in Ford Pro Intelligence. Parts of revenue growth this year has been driven by double-digit growth in our U.S. wholesale channel and the expansion of our retail and wholesale businesses in Europe. We are also increasing dealer service retention with digital and uptime tools to drive organic parts growth. We are excited about the prospects these auto adjacencies offer for continued accretive growth. Now, looking ahead to our full-year 2026 outlook.
We are confident in our full-year trajectory and our planned investment cadence, and now expect full-year adjusted EBIT between $10.5 billion-$11 billion. Adjusted free cash flow and capital expenditures are unchanged, at $6 billion-$7 billion and $9.5 billion-$10.5 billion respectively. Our guidance does not include potential impacts of a significant escalation in the Middle East or a material downturn in the U.S. economy, which, if either or both occurred, could have a substantial impact on industry demand. For our full-year segment outlook, we expect Ford Blue EBIT of about $5.5 billion, Ford Pro EBIT of about $7 billion, Model e losses remain unchanged at about $4 billion, and Ford Credit EBT updated to about $2.8 billion.
Our guidance now assumes a U.S. SAAR of 16.5 million units, commodity headwinds approaching $2.5 billion year-over-year, an increase of about $50
